title: Algebra coactions over commutative rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $C$ a commutative Hopf $R$-algebra with comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\epsilon$, and $E$ a commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. An algebra coaction is an $R$-algebra map $\rho:E\to E\otimes_R C$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] satisfying $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_E$ and $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$, with the standard tensor unit and associativity identifications. For an affine group scheme $G$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-group-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], its algebra coactions are those for the canonical coordinate Hopf algebra $C=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ [def-sfb-affine-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. Scalar extension of $G$ uses the group law transported by the pullback functor [def-pc-base-change]; its structure morphism remains affine. The canonical coordinate Hopf structure on a bundled group is exposed for typeclass inference. No field, finite-generation, flatness or nonzero-algebra assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5, affine algebra actions, pp.522--523; Proposition 9.3.1(i), p.524; https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf
